subject: Tenant data exposure — IR plan request & evidence exchange
messages:
From: security@acme-ops.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@acme.com, cloudops@vendor-corp.net
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible tenant data exposure — immediate IR info requested

Hi Marissa,

We detected an anomalous object ACL change in an S3 bucket that looks like it could have exposed a small set of tenant configuration files (customer IDs only, no PII observed yet). Our detection flagged the change at ~2026-10-29T06:40Z. We alerted our SOC and are performing containment on our side, but given the integration with Redwood's inference routing we need your IR group to confirm:

- Whether any request from Acme tenants was proxied through Redwood in that window (06:00–07:00Z).
- If Redwood captured any request/response telemetry or API keys tied to those requests.
- A copy of your Incident Response Plan (IRP) high-level steps and the contact for your on-call forensics lead.

Can you also provide a redacted IR plan and any SOC 2 / SIG evidence we can use to demonstrate controls to our auditors? We need an initial response within 4 hours and an evidence handoff by EOD if possible.

We have opened a ticket on our side (ACME-9872).

Thanks,
Asha Raman
SecOps Lead, Acme Logistics
security@acme-ops.com

Attachments: None
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: security@acme-ops.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible tenant data exposure — immediate IR info requested

Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the worry here. We take exposures seriously; I'm triaging this with our on-call forensics team now (cc'ed).

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Placing a temporary routing block on requests between 06:00–07:30Z UTC for the affected routing group to stop any further proxying.
- Preserving KV caches and request traces for the window you called out. I have asked infra to snapshot relevant GPU node telemetry and request logs.
- Starting a scoped log extraction for the tenant IDs you referenced. Jonas will follow up with exact extraction artifacts and format.

What we'll deliver within the next 8 hours:
- A redacted IR plan (high level) and a SOC 2 / SIG evidence index (control crosswalk) for your auditors.
- Telemetry snapshot (redacted) showing proxied request IDs and timestamps.
- Point of contact for forensics and a proposed cadence for a 30-minute bridge to review artifacts.

Request for you: please share any sample request IDs or object keys you have (redact tenant identifiers where needed) so we can speed reconciliation.

I'll send the redacted IR plan as an attachment as soon as it's ready.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0193

Attachments: None (will follow)

Marissa / Asha — quick technical note from forensics:

We're preparing a telemetry package. To make sure the extract contains only what you need, please confirm the object key prefixes and approximate requester IPs you saw. If you don't have prefixes, provide a couple of example object names or approximate time slices; we'll filter down.

What we'll attach in the telemetry snapshot: request timestamps, proxied request IDs, headers (redacted per our privacy policy), and SHA256 checksums of the served objects. We will NOT include full object bodies unless you expressly request them and complete an evidence-handback agreement.

Preliminary attachment: telemetry_snapshot.zip (contains log-samples and extraction manifest).

Jonas Weber
Principal Forensics Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Possible tenant data exposure — IR plan, SIG/CAIQ responses, and postmortem readout

Asha / Acme team — attaching the materials we discussed. Thank you for your patience while we completed redaction review.

Attachments included (redacted where appropriate):
- ir_plan_redacted.pdf — high-level IR steps, escalation contacts, and evidence handling procedures. Sensitive internal runbook snippets removed per contract.
- SIG-CAIQ-responses.xlsx — our completed SIG / CAIQ responses with control references and evidence pointers.
- telemetry_snapshot.zip — sample logs and an extraction manifest (manifest includes checksums and filtering criteria).

Actions we took (summary):
- Containment: temporary routing block (06:00–07:30Z) and removal of an overly permissive object ACL that caused the exposure.
- Preservation: snapshots of request logs and KV cache preserved; hashes captured for each relevant object.
- Root cause: preliminary analysis shows a deployment automation script mistakenly applied a broad ACL; we are rolling a fix to our deployment pipeline to enforce prefix-scoped ACLs.
- Customer notification: we recommend you notify affected tenants as you see fit; we will provide sanitized timelines and proof-of-hash for any tenant you identify.

Proposed next steps and readout:
- 30-minute bridge to review artifacts and walk through the IR plan: Mon 2026-11-01 10:00 PT / 17:00 UTC. Please confirm availability.
- Postmortem: we'll compile a formal postmortem document by 2026-11-05 and share a redacted copy suitable for auditor review.

If you want full object contents for forensic review, we require a signed evidence-handback addendum; we can start that process on the bridge.

HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.redwood.company/ticket/RED-4321
Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.redwood.company/teams/security/ACME-IR-2026

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
